correctness.rationale: Correct for every existing finite projective plane of order q>=2, including non-Desarguesian. A proper color class dominated by an open neighborhood must lie entirely in one incidence bipartition side. Each point-side color class has supporting line, so an m=q+1 cover of points is minimum by union ≤rq+1; equality forces the entire concurrent pencil. Dually line classes supported by all points on ℓ. For q>=2, every point-side class contains at least two off-center points identifying its unique supporting line, and the center P chooses exactly one m class. Dual geometry gives independent ℓ and one chosen point X*. Thus unlabeled optima v²m² and named optima (2m)!v²m², v=q²+q+1. Under one-vertex optimum recoloring, only P and ℓ can move; each (P,ℓ) fixed component is K_m □ K_m; named classes further separate label associations. Independent q=2 exhaustive direct dominated partitions give 21 one-side optima, 441 two-side, 49 components, agreeing with theorem. The q=3 original package additionally supplies independent exhaustive/constructive programs; finite tests do not prove all-order result.
